text:
Jamie (Design): quick microcopy nit — the confirmation tooltip on the rollout page currently says "Stop rollout" and the modal close button aria-label is just "Dismiss". Felt ambiguous for screen readers.

Jamie (Design): screenshot: `.../rollouts/stop-tooltip.png` (just FYI)

Miguel R: strong agree on ambiguity. For destructive flows we should be explicit about consequence. Tooltip could say something like: "Stop rollout now — will halt and optionally revert instances".

Elaine P: accessibility note: aria-labels should identify the action + target. e.g. `aria-label="Stop rollout for <service-name>"`. Avoid adding status words like "destructive" or parentheses — screen readers read punctuation oddly.

Miguel R: also seeing a keyboard issue: after hitting Stop the focus stays behind the modal, so keyboard users don't land on the dialog header. That's a11y-blocking.

Jamie (Design): good catch. For copy tense: prefer present-tense verbs on CTAs, so keep "Stop rollout" (not "Stopping rollout" or "Stoping—typo"). For the inline tooltip copy maybe be shorter: "Stop rollout and revert" vs long sentence. Thoughts?

Elaine P: shorter is fine if the modal body expands on consequences and `aria-describedby` points to that paragraph. Modal should be `role="alertdialog"` and trap focus.

Miguel R: implementation suggestion: button text = "Stop rollout", aria-label = "Stop rollout for <service-name>", modal paragraph id = "stop-rollout-desc" then `aria-describedby="stop-rollout-desc"`. Fix the focus trap in the same ticket.

Jamie (Design): I'll update the Figma copy and open a small PR with the tooltip text + modal copy + recommended a11y attributes. Will tag you both.

Miguel R: I'll own the focus trap fix and add the a11y checklist items to the ticket.

ux-bot: Accessibility checklist: https://internal.redwood/a11y/checklist — added `keyboard-focus` and `aria-describedby` to the task.

Jamie (Design): great, thanks :thumbsup: I'll push copy change to the design branch today and link the PR here.
